Untrack makes agent manage leave sessions out of its view. Nothing is
deleted: the transcript stays where its harness keeps it, the harness can
still resume it, and agent sessions still lists it. "agent manage track"
brings a session back, and "agent manage view --untracked" shows them.

Name sessions as HARNESS:ID (claude:3f3a9c..., as the view's JSON keys
them) or by an id or the start of one, if only one session has it. Or pick
them by what they are, with any of:
  --state S[,S]      running, dormant, ended, missing, unknown
  --older-than WHEN  not written since: a duration back from now (30d, 2w,
                     12h) or a local date (2026-11-01)
  --harness H        claude, agy, kimi
  --stale            flagged stale (see agent manage view)
A subagent's session goes with the session that started it.

A running session is never untracked unless it is named and --force is
given. --dry-run lists what would be untracked and changes nothing.

An agent's own record is a different thing: "agent cleanup <name>" removes
an ended agent. Untracking its sessions doesn't.

Usage:
  agent manage untrack [session...] [flags]

Examples:
  agent manage untrack claude:3f3a9c12-88aa-4c0e-9a51-0f6f0c1d2e3f
  agent manage untrack 3f3a9c
  agent manage untrack --state ended,dormant --older-than 30d --dry-run

Flags:
      --dry-run             List what would be untracked; change nothing
      --force               Untrack a named session even though it is running
      --harness string      Only this harness's sessions: claude, agy, kimi
  -h, --help                help for untrack
      --older-than string   Only sessions not written since then: a duration back from now (30d, 2w) or a local date
      --stale               Only sessions flagged stale (not running, not written for 14 days)
      --state string        Only sessions in one of these states: running, dormant, ended, missing, unknown

Global Flags:
      --backend string          Backend for spawn or adopt: claude, aider, agy, or shell (spawn requires it or --backend-config; adopt auto-detects)
      --backend-config string   JSON file defining a custom backend (or app settings); pass it again to status/wait/watch for agents spawned with it
  -q, --quiet                   Don't print hints (results and errors still print)
      --termd-ns string         g3d-termd namespace (default: agents; never default or wall)
